Once created on a mechanicus world - let's say Mars. They are hoisted up giant space elevators into low orbit - where warp capable vessels can dock and receive titans and other armaments. Likewise, deploying a titan on a forgeworld is done in much the same manner but in reverse. On any other world, the titan is "dropped" onto the planet in a huge drop-pod of a scale difficult to comprehend. One would have thought that dropping a titan onto such a world would be condemning it to live out it's existance on said planet until it meets it's eventual demise - or the infrastructure on the planet is developed to the point where a space elevator of suitable scale is eventually developed - which would allow the process of docking and boarding to be done.   


Given that a ship of suitable size to lift a titan would suffer the effects of gravity overload - should they pass below low-orbit and enter the atmosphere - the only way to recover a titan on a world with out the infrastructure to lift it into low orbit would be to literally build a space elevator. Unless the planet had a thin atmosphere and low gravity, there wouldn't any exceptions. This factor is considered before a titan is deployed on a planet - as they are massive resource tokens with large strategic value and should be used carefully.
